title: Slack Notifications Not Working: How to Fix It
body_md:
![Slack Help Center page showing how to troubleshoot Slack notifications](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/slack-notifications-not-working-how-to-fix-it/1.png)
*Slack's official Troubleshoot Slack notifications help page ([source](https://slack.com/help/articles/360001559367-Troubleshoot-Slack-notifications))*

**The fastest fix:** check whether notifications are paused, and confirm delivery is actually enabled in Slack's own preferences. Slack's own advice is to look for a snooze icon next to your name — if it's there, notifications are paused and you need to resume them. On desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar, select Preferences, then Notifications, and under "How to notify you," make sure Desktop notifications or Mobile notifications is ticked — if the box for that device is unticked, that device gets nothing.

If that's already set correctly, work down the list below.

## Why This Happens

Slack notifications pass through several independent gates, and any one of them can quietly block an alert:

- **Paused notifications or a notification schedule** you set weeks ago and forgot about.
- **Workspace-level preferences** set to mentions and direct messages only instead of everything. The menu offers Everything or Mentions and direct messages (@you, @channel, @here) — with the second, ordinary channel messages never alert you.
- **Channel-level overrides.** You can set notification preferences for specific channels and group DMs with three or more people to change what messages notify you. Channel-level settings beat global ones, so a muted channel ignores everything you set above it.
- **Your operating system.** macOS Focus modes and Windows Focus/Do Not Disturb can suppress Slack even when Slack itself is configured perfectly.
- **Mobile timing settings.** By default, Slack delays mobile notifications while you're active on desktop.
- **Battery savers and "optimization" apps.** On Android, if Slack's battery usage is set to Restricted or Optimized, the system kills its background connection and notifications stop arriving — Settings → Apps → Slack → Battery, set to Unrestricted.
- **A stale local cache or an out-of-date app.** An old app version can lose its push registration.

One more thing worth knowing if you use Slack in a browser: notifications only arrive for workspaces you have open in a browser tab, and the browser itself has to have granted permission.

## Step-by-Step Fixes

### 1. Resume paused notifications

Click your profile picture in the sidebar and look for the snooze icon or "Notifications paused." If it's active, resume notifications. While you're there, check whether you have a recurring notification schedule that's running longer than you intended.

### 2. Check your global notification preferences

Profile picture → **Preferences** → **Notifications**. Set what to notify you about to everything temporarily — that confirms whether a too-narrow setting was the problem, then narrow it back down. If you only want pings for @-mentions, that's fine — just know that's why quiet channels stay quiet.

Also check **Sound & appearance** in the same panel. That's where you control message previews in notifications and whether all Slack sounds are muted. If you're seeing banners but hearing nothing, start there.

### 3. Check the specific channel or DM

If only *one* conversation is silent, it's a channel-level override, not a global problem. Click the channel name at the top, open the Notifications dropdown and make sure it isn't set to Mute. On mobile, open the conversation, tap its name, then Notifications, and pick your preference.

### 4. Check your OS notification settings

- **macOS:** System Settings → Notifications → Slack, enable Allow Notifications and choose Banners or Alerts. Then check Control Center for an active Focus mode — Focus has its own allowed-apps list.
- **Windows:** Settings → System → Notifications. Confirm notifications from apps are enabled overall, then find Slack in the list and check it's on. Also check that Focus assist / Do Not Disturb isn't running on a schedule.
- **iPhone:** Settings → Notifications → Slack. Also check Background App Refresh is on for Slack.
- **Android:** Settings → Apps → Slack → Notifications, turned on including the message and mention categories, and battery usage set to Unrestricted.

### 5. Fix delayed mobile notifications

If pings arrive but arrive late, check the delivery settings before assuming there's an outage. In the mobile app, tap your profile picture, tap Notifications, tap **Notify Me on Mobile** and set it to **As soon as I'm inactive** for the fastest delivery. There's also an "Immediately, even if I'm active" option, which is the one to pick if you often walk away from an open laptop.

### 6. Run Slack's built-in diagnostic (mobile)

Slack ships a real test tool, and it's underused. Slack's own guidance: if you've checked your mobile notification settings and are still having trouble, run a diagnostic test from the app and send the results in for more help. Find it at profile picture → **Notifications** → **Troubleshoot Notifications**. If the test passes every stage but no test notification actually lands, reinstalling the app and running it again is the next step, since that re-registers the device for push.

### 7. Clear stuck badges

Different problem, different fix. If you see notification badges for conversations you've already read, or your Threads view won't unbold, something might be out of sync on Slack's end. Open the affected workspace in the desktop app or browser and press Shift + Esc to mark everything read.

### 8. Escalate to Slack

If nothing lands, send the diagnostic results in: tap Send a report in the Troubleshoot Notifications screen and include a short description of the problem. Slack asks that you include a brief summary of the issue as well as your workspace URL and email address in the request.

Before you escalate, it's worth ruling out a service-side problem. Check status.slack.com if notifications fail for everyone at once.

## How to Prevent It Next Time

- **Audit your pause and schedule settings monthly.** A forgotten notification schedule can suppress alerts for hours a day.
- **Use mute deliberately.** Mute high-volume channels instead of dialing down your global settings — that way your important channels keep working.
- **Add Slack to your Focus mode allowlist** on macOS and iOS rather than relying on the general notification toggle.
- **Keep the app updated** and skip aggressive battery-saver apps on your work phone.
- **Set each device on purpose.** Slack has a separate "Use different settings for my mobile devices" option, so your phone can be quietly running rules you never set on desktop.

*Updated October 2026: this guide is written from Slack's published documentation and public reports, not from a controlled diagnostic test on my own machines. Menu names in Slack's notification preferences have shifted over the past couple of years, so what you see may be worded slightly differently.*

## My Take

My read is that most "Slack notifications not working" cases aren't bugs at all. They're three or four layers of settings — Slack's global preferences, a channel override, an OS Focus mode, and a battery optimizer — each of which looks fine on its own. Slack's documentation treats these as a checklist, and that's exactly the problem: nothing tells you which layer is failing.

So the single thing I'd do first is send yourself a DM from another account, or ask a colleague to. A DM bypasses channel mutes and bypasses the "mentions only" global setting. If that lands and channel messages don't, you've got a Slack-side preference. If nothing lands anywhere, it's the OS or the device. That one test cuts the search space in half before you touch a single menu.

I also think Slack deserves credit for shipping the mobile Troubleshoot Notifications tool, which is more than most apps do. The fair point against my framing: Slack is genuinely hard to get right here, because iOS and Android both aggressively police background push, and Slack can't control what the OS throws away.

The setting I'd change permanently, if notifications matter to your job, is the mobile delay. Slack's default of holding mobile pings until you're inactive on desktop is sensible for people at a desk and actively harmful if you're the on-call person who walks away from an unlocked laptop. Set it to notify immediately and mute the channels you don't need instead.

And a boring warning worth stating plainly: if you work somewhere with compliance or device-management rules, don't start uninstalling apps or disabling OS security features to chase this. I'm not an IT or legal professional, and on a managed work device the notification policy may not be yours to change — ask your admin before you fight it.
